source.publication: 2025 Oklahoma Resident Individual Income Tax Forms and Instructions (Form 511 packet)
source.section: Form 511 lines 1-14 and 18 (PDF pages 42-43); select line instructions (PDF pages 9-10); standard deduction line 10 (PDF page 10); exemptions line 11 and the Regular exemption terms (PDF pages 8 and 10); Tax Table (PDF pages 27-38); Special exemption and Sixty-five or older (PDF page 9)

worked: Federal AGI = wages (you) 13,850.00 + Roth conversion (you) 20,000.00 = 33,850.00. Federal taxable income = 33,850.00 - standard deduction 17,750.00 (15,750.00 + 1 x 2,000.00 for 65 or older) = 16,100.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Oklahoma starts from federal AGI). Form 511: line 1 federal AGI 33,850.00; line 2 subtractions 0.00; line 3 = 33,850.00 - 0.00 = 33,850.00; line 4 out-of-state income 0.00; line 5 33,850.00; line 6 additions 0.00; line 7 Oklahoma AGI 33,850.00; line 8 adjustments 0.00; line 9 33,850.00; line 10 standard deduction (single) 6,350.00; line 11 exemptions: 1 Regular + 0 Special = 1 x 1,000.00 = 1,000.00 (1 person(s) 65 or older; line 1 33,850.00 is over the 15,000.00 limit, so 0 Special); line 12 = 6,350.00 + 1,000.00 = 7,350.00; line 13 taxable income = 33,850.00 - 7,350.00 = 26,500.00; line 14 tax (the projection's brackets as numbers; the booklet prints only a table and worksheets): 0.25% x 1,000.00 = 2.5000 + 0.75% x 1,500.00 = 11.2500 + 1.75% x 1,250.00 = 21.8750 + 2.75% x 1,150.00 = 31.6250 + 3.75% x 2,300.00 = 86.2500 + 4.75% x 19,300.00 = 916.7500; total 1,070.2500 = 1,070.25. Line 13 is under 100,000, so the form reads the tax table: row 26,500-26,550, column 'Single or married filing separate', PDF page 30, gives 1,071; expected keeps the schedule figure. Lines 15-17 credits 0.00; line 18 income tax 1,070.25. The projection tests line 1 with the conversion in it, 33,850.00, so no Special exemption. The booklet leaves conversion income out of the test: 13,850.00 is within 15,000.00, line 11 would be 2,000.00 and tax 47.50 less.
accepted_approximations: The brackets are derived from the printed tax table and the 100,000-and-over worksheets; the booklet prints no schedule. Below 100,000 tax is figured on the exact income, where the booklet taxes each 50-dollar row at its midpoint and rounds. At 100,000 and over the single and separate worksheet starts from 4,562 where the schedule gives 4,561.50.

The age 65 exemption's limits are tested on Federal AGI including Roth conversion income; the booklet leaves conversion income out of the test, and a projection's measures cannot subtract it. A filer whose income is within the limit only without the conversion loses the exemption here.

Roth conversions are left out of line 6 (covers_unclear in the record: the booklet says conversions are taxed in the same year as federally and does not say whether they count as retirement benefits). If Oklahoma counts them, this overstates tax for a converter.
